Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1179
Claimant:
Nathan Velasquez
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
April 17, 2025
Claim opened after the claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot and a neck injury diagnosed as
whiplash. The claimant is not represented by an attorney, so all contact will be direct.
April 18, 2025
Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the vehicles made contact in the lot the way the claimant described. Both
parties agree on the sequence of events.
April 25, 2025
Obtained statements from two witnesses and photos of both vehicles. The witnesses and photos match the reported
impact, and the damage appears largely consistent with it.
May 17, 2025
Police report lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time of the collision, which matches the claimant's
account. The policyholder confirmed the driver lives in the household and is listed as a covered member.
May 18, 2025
The claimant's medical records show treatment that followed a typical course for this type of injury, with visits tapering
off as symptoms improved. No prior injury to the neck or upper back appaers in the records.
June 16, 2025
Prior-loss records turned up a claim involving major damage to the same areas of the vehicle from an earlier accident
that was never reported to us. The curernt claim presents that damage as new, so this needs to be reconciled before
any payment decision.
August 12, 2025
The claimant later added a few smaller details, such as the position of the other car and how long the vehicles stayed
in contact, but the core account has not changed. Nothing in the file suggests the damage happened before the
policy's coverage start date.
September 14, 2025
Reviewed the file and noted the open question about the earlier unreported damage. Next step is to request the prior
repair estimate and speak with the claimant about that history before closing the injury and property portions of the
claim.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
